Q2 NOT FLAKY: assert runs on POST-threshold entities (server applies ja thresholds by default). The path is deterministic given the pinned model+thresholds file, proven by test_ja_parity_operating_point pinning operating-point F1 to metrics.json at abs=1e-6. rest-api-spec.md documents this exact sentence yielding 2 spans (PER 織田信長 + LOC 東京都千代田区), both high-confidence canonical entities; assert needs only >=1, so margin is 2. Independently reproduced: pytest tests/server/test_live_server.py -m live -> 3 passed (test_ner_single_live PASSED with the new assert), confirming the model actually emits entities. The test is skipif-gated on model-dir presence, so no false positive in model-less CI. It fails only if a canonical sentence yields zero entities -- the exact regression it is meant to catch (correct design, not flakiness).

MINOR: phobert EVT inflation: summary json says 3.99pp, actual calculation is 3.98pp (3.984pp). Root cause: summary rounds per-entity F1 to 4dp first, then subtracts. Report text says '+4.0' (further rounded) — not a measurement error, just rounding cascade. All three representations (3.98/3.99/4.0) are internally consistent with their respective precision levels.

MINOR: unique_orig in summary json = 29,337 (from pii_all.jsonl), benchmark.md/history.md say '29,343개' (from all.jsonl unique texts). These refer to DIFFERENT source files and are both factually correct in context. Not a discrepancy.

However the header (line 5: 'pii_all.jsonl (중복 제거 후 38,371 행)') describes the current file incorrectly — the file is now 37,706 rows. This was not introduced by the two commits under review.

WEAKNESS (non-blocking): The pooled_metrics.json on disk was REGENERATED at 18:50 today, ~3h after the #133 merge (15:51) and after fold0 (16:54). So the artifact now holds the FRESH-retrain numbers (EVT 0.8159 etc.), while the #133-recorded canonical (EVT 0.8249) survives only in prose. Consequence: benchmark.md still headlines 'current canonical model = evtfix ... EVT 0.8249' (line 12) while this new spec headlines EVT 0.8159 — the docs/reports series now carries TWO different 'canonical' EVT numbers across files. The spec's reconciliation note (lines 103-109) is honest about this and ties both to the same JSON+noise, so it is not measurement fraud, but the cross-file headline divergence (0.8249 vs 0.8159) is a real consistency snag a reader could trip on. Recommend: either (i) refresh benchmark.md/history.md headlines to the new pooled numbers, or (ii) have the spec explicitly state it supersedes the #133 headline. Not a FAIL because the spec's own numbers are 100%% JSON-backed and the divergence is disclosed.

TRAIN-SEED NOISE EXACT: doc 0.641-0.707 swing ~0.066 == recomputed m100_ts1=0.7067, ts7=0.7052, ts42=0.6413, swing 0.0654. Match. But swing (0.065) >> 0.012 by 5x, so the order-of-magnitude argument survives the caveat.

HALLUCINATION qualitative claim SUPPORTED: all 4 cited examples (어성초/SM5/에이리언1/영웅본색) present in clean_prod_fnfp/fp_top_PROD.md as gold-empty HALLUCINATION FPs. The ~half-gold-omission claim is conservative-to-low: of 31 HALL FPs, ~24 are plausibly real products/works (only se/라/오/방화/사드 etc are noise/over-firing). ~half UNDER-states the real fraction, so it does not inflate the gold-incompleteness argument.

DEFECT (must-fix, non-blocking): the ~46% structural-fraction figure is NOT reproducible under any single consistent counting convention. Doc writes eponymy(55)+boundary(26)=~46% of errors. 55 = TYPE_MISMATCH both-sides (FN24+FP31); 26 = BOUNDARY ONE side only (table shows FN26|FP26=52). Denominator 175 = FN87+FP88 = both-sides. Mixing both-sides eponymy(55) with one-side boundary(26) gives 81/175=0.463; the consistent both-sides figure is (55+52)/175=0.611=~61%. The 46% is an inconsistent-convention artifact.

DEFECT IMPACT IS CONSERVATIVE (why non-blocking): the true both-sides structural mass (~61%) is LARGER than the doc claim (~46%). The deliverable conclusion is structural-ceiling / data-cannot-fix / external-data-needed. A larger structural share strengthens that conclusion, so the arithmetic slip understates rather than inflates the case. It does not flip the verdict on the gate (A) ceiling 0.724 nor (C) integrity. CRITICAL/HIGH-confidence: src/server/translate.py:_mask assumes non-overlapping PII spans and replaces right-to-left using ORIGINAL text offsets for every span; when two client-supplied PII spans overlap (e.g. ID_NUM span 3-13 and CREDIT_CARD span 8-24 on the same text), the second replacement slices the ALREADY-MUTATED string at stale offsets. The /v1/translate endpoint does not validate/reject overlapping or malformed spans before calling _mask.

HIGH-confidence: src/server/translate.py:_restore unconditionally strips ANY leftover 【N】-shaped token via _SENTINEL_RE.sub('', out) after replacing known sentinels, without checking whether that token was actually one _mask inserted. Japanese text commonly uses lenticular brackets for headers/enumerations (e.g. 【重要】, 【1】【2】). Reproduced two failure modes: (1) pre-existing '【9】' unrelated to any PII silently vanishes from the translated output (content loss/corruption, contradicts the documented invariant 'sentinel 소실 시 부재이되 훼손 없음'); (2) when the coincidental bracket index equals an active PII sentinel id (e.g. text already contains literal '【0】' while PII is masked as index 0), _restore's naive str.replace(token, value) replaces BOTH occurrences, injecting the real PII value into an unrelated part of the sentence ('手順【0】を確認...' -> '手順010-1234-5678を確認...'). This is exactly the '원문에 이미 【숫자】 패턴이 있는 경우' edge case the review brief called out, and it is a realistic collision given 【】 is a standard JA typographic convention, not a contrived input.
